content.text:
The Tailwind docs don't cover prettier-plugin-tailwindcss's internal sorting algorithm (that plugin lives in a separate repo, not indexed here). The most relevant match is `tailwind-css/src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx:69`, which explains the general limitation:

> "Since Tailwind scans your source files as plain text, it has no way of understanding string concatenation or interpolation in the programming language you're using."

This is exactly the underlying reason for the behavior reported: the plugin treats each literal segment between `${...}` interpolations as an isolated chunk of text, since it can't know what the interpolated value will resolve to (it could be a partial class name like `bg-` + `red-600`). So it only sorts classes *within* each segment, not across the whole template — this is expected/by-design behavior, not a misconfiguration.
